newsitem.title: USA: NY state asks companies to act on teen tobacco use.
newsitem.headline: NY state asks companies to act on teen tobacco use.

text.p: The New York State comptroller, who runs the state's $75 billion pension fund, on Wednesday said he had proposed shareholder resolutions to four tobacco firms, asking them to help curb tobacco use by teenagers.
The state's Common Retirement Fund holds a total of 6.5 million shares in Phillip Morris Cos Inc, Loews Corp, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp and UST Inc, a holding that is valued at nearly $500 million.
The resolution asks the boards of the four companies to voluntarily implement marketing restrictions to curb teen smoking and young people's access to tobacco products.

Saying a national health crisis must be confronted, H. Carl McCall, in prepared remarks, said "As a shareholder, I'm concerned about the volatility this has caused in the value of our holdings. I urge these companies, from a financial standpoint and as good corporate citizens, to help protect the health of our children."
In March, McCall told the fund's advisory council he had ordered managers of non-indexed portfolios to freeze their current holdings of tobacco stocks.

Eighteen state attorneys general, New York City and the California cities of San Francisco and San Jose and counties, including Los Angeles, have sued the tobacco industry to recoup health care costs of smokers.
